test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 14 March, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

P. American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965

Q. the problems of collective action were popularized by the

R. that coercion or some other device must be present in order

S. for a group of individuals to act in their common interest
solution:
Here the correct answer is **QPRS**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this arrangement, the sentence starts with the introduction of the problems of collective action being popularized. This provides the context for the subsequent parts.
 
 
• **Q. **"The problems of collective action were popularized by the"
 
• **P. **"American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965"
 
 
 
• These two parts go together as they establish who popularized the problems of collective action and when it happened. Mancur Olson, an American political economist, is mentioned as the individual responsible for bringing attention to these problems through his writing in 1965.
 
 
• **R.** "that coercion or some other device must be present in order"
 
• **S.** "for a group of individuals to act in their common interest"
 
 
 
• The last two parts connect to form a logical explanation. It states that in order for a group of individuals to act in their common interest, coercion or some other mechanism is necessary. This concludes the sentence by providing a solution or conclusion related to the problems of collective action.
 
• By following the order **QPRS**, the sentence maintains a logical flow by introducing the problem, establishing the authority, and providing an explanation or solution.

 

**Correct Arrangement**__: *The problems of collective action were popularized by the American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965 that coercion or some other device must be present in order for a group of individuals to act in their common interest.*
